items.title: George Wein — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I took Monk. I went to Thelonious... I said I want to take him to Europe... I just hung out with Thelonious and I made him feel good. He played... I'd drive him and Nellie home

ctx.x: Any memories of nights when you just thought, Oh my god, what am I ever gonna do now? Or something happened and you had to just scramble?

Well, it's happened twice in my life. The first one was 1960 and 1971 in Newport when the kids broke the fences down. But you go home that night and you think, What am I gonna do now? Charlie Rouse, after the '60 … I took Monk. I went to Thelonious and I went to his manager and nobody would touch Thelonious, nobody. They didn't want to know him. And I said I want to take him to Europe. I had to guarantee the money to the promoters that were buying, because Monk's reputation was so bad. But when I went to Europe,…
We started talking about what are you ever gonna do.
